thread.title: Market Structure Is Still Broken - SPDR S&P 500 Trust ETF (NYSEARCA:SPY)

author: KCI Research Ltd.
title: Market Structure Is Still Broken - SPDR S&P 500 Trust ETF (NYSEARCA:SPY)
text:
A 60:40 allocation to passive long-only equities and bonds has been a great proposition for the last 35 years… We are profoundly worried that this could be a risky allocation over the next 10."
Sanford C. Bernstein & Company Analysts (January 2017)
Bull markets are born on pessimism, grow on skepticism, mature on optimism, and die on euphoria"
Sir John Templeton
Life and investing are long ballgames."
Julian Robertson
( Photo Source )
Introduction Previously, I have written how the market structure is broken, specifically, in this article, " Be Prepared For A Crash - Part II ", and while crowded trades have started to unwind, the structure of the market is still broken, and we can see this when sifting through the performance breakdown of the S&P 500 constituents.
What do I mean?
Let me explain.
Investment Thesis Think of the financial market, specifically the current equity markets, like a funnel, where liquidity is funneled to the equities that outperform. What happens when liquidity is taken out? Where should it come from? Where is it coming from? These are key investment questions today, as the reappearance of price discovery has profound impact for the crowded long and short trades.
S&P 500 Index Performance YTD The S&P 500 Index, as measured by the SPDR S&P 500 ETF ( SPY ) is up still up 2.4% this year, in 2018, through the close of the market on Thursday, December 6th, even after the recent declines in October, and now in December.
(Source: Author, StockCharts.com )
For reference, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, as measured by SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF ( DIA ), is up 2.8% YTD.
(Source: Author, StockCharts.com )
Additionally, the Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ), a compilation of the top-100 NASDAQ companies, is up 7.4% YTD.
(Source: Author, StockCharts.com )
Thus, while almost all of the rest of the world has struggled in 2018, epitomized by the performance of the iShares MSCI Germany ETF ( EWG ), which is down -19.0% YTD, U.S. equities, which are admittedly off of their earlier year highs, have been the outlier, delivering positive performance is a sea of proverbial red.
(Source: Author, StockCharts.com )
Building on the point above, U.S. equities have outperformed, specifically, large capitalization U.S. equities, buoyed by both domestic and global capital flows that still see the largest U.S. companies as safe-havens, in a market structure where passive fund flows still rule the roost.
Biggest Companies In The S&P 500 Drive Performance The top twenty equities by U.S. market capitalization are Microsoft ( MSFT ), Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.A ), ( BRK.B ), Alphabet ( GOOGL ), ( GOOG ), Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ), J.P. Morgan Chase ( JPM ), Facebook ( FB ), Exxon Mobil ( XOM ), Unitedhealth Group ( UNH ), Pfizer ( PFE ), Visa ( V ), Bank of America ( BAC ), Verizon ( VZ ), Procter & Gamble ( PG ), Intel ( INTC ), Chevron ( CVX ), AT&T ( T ), Wells Fargo ( WFC ), and Cisco Systems ( CSCO ).
A handful of these equities have driven the positive performance in the broader market indices, specifically Microsoft, Amazon, Unitedhealth, Pfizer, Visa, Verizon, and Cisco the 1st, 3rd, 10th, 11th, 12th, 14th, and 20th largest companies, respectively by market capitalization, with each of these companies sporting double-digit percentage gains as of this writing.
Collectively, these aforementioned companies comprise roughly 12.2% of the S&P 500 Index, according to data from Morningstar ( MORN ), with Microsoft having a 3.7% S&P 500 Index weight, Amazon a 3.1% weighting, Unitedhealth a 1.2% weighting, Pfizer a 1.2% weighting, Visa a 1.1%, Verizon a 1.1% weighting, and Cisco a 1.0% weighting (all the weightings are rounded).
In terms of year-to-date returns, here are the year-to-date performance charts for MSFT, AMZN, UNH, PFE, V, VZ, and CSCO.
(Source: Author, StockCharts.com )
Looking at the charts above, MSFT is up 29.9% YTD in 2018, AMZN is up 45.3% in 2018, UNH is up 27.3% YTD, PFE is up 28.6% YTD, V is up 24.5% YTD, VZ is up 15.0% YTD, and CSCO is up 30.2% YTD.
These seven companies, which again represent the double-digit gainers in the top-20 S&P 500 Index components YTD, are responsible for roughly 3.9% of the return of the S&P 500 YTD in 2018, with Microsoft and Amazon representing 2.5% of the S&P 500's YTD return. Now keep in mind that the S&P 500 on a total return basis is only up 2.4% for the year in 2018, so without the performance of these seven companies, the S&P 500 Index would be negative year-to-date.
Going further, without the positive performance contributions of Microsoft, and Amazon, two performance standouts in 2018, and in the current bull market dating to March 9th, 2009, the S&P 500 Index would be negative year-to-date.
Negative Performance In Top 20 S&P 500 Index Components Is Rare, So Far Which of the top-20 companies in the S&P 500 Index are materially negative, in terms of year-to-date performance?
Take a minute...can you guess.
Okay, the negative performers that stand out year-to-date, specifically those with double-digit negative performance are Facebook, with a S&P 500 weighting of roughly 1.5%, AT&T, with a weighting of roughly 1.0%, and Wells Fargo, with a index weighting of roughly 1.0%. Here is the YTD performance of these three equities.
(Source: Author, StockCharts.com )
Looking at the YTD performance charts above, Facebook, the 7th largest S&P 500 component, is down -20.9% YTD, AT&T, the 18th largest S&P 500 component, is down -16.8% YTD, and Wells Fargo, the 19th largest S&P 500 Index component is down -13.3% YTD.
Collectively, these companies have been responsible for roughly a -0.6% contribution to the S&P 500 returns, which is a small negative drag compared to the positive 3.9% tailwind provided by the top YTD gainers in the S&P 500 Index.
Closing Thoughts The funnel is still in-tact, with domestic and global capital flows continuing to be directed to the largest S&P 500 companies, as evidenced by the performance breakdown of the top-20 S&P 500 constituents.
If and when the S&P 500 Index actually goes negative on a year-to-date basis, capital flows, led by passive index flows, and trend followers, will actually hit the largest S&P 500 constituents the hardest, as these companies will be sources of liquidity.
We are not there yet, and we have a long way to go in our journey to rediscover price discovery.
To close, even though it has been a very difficult stretch for active, value-oriented investors, I think we are about to enter a golden age for active, value investors , and the most out-of-favor sectors, and the most out-of-favor equities will be at the forefront of this opportunity.
